audit.whatIsWrong: Seven strings call Ntofo Strikes (Q) a knockup that interrupts your dash chain. Riot's text says Q damages and slows in a line, and at 2 stacks fires a shockwave that PULLS enemies in — the opposite direction. The knockback and stun live on Path Maker (W) and All Out (R). Footwork (E) grants a shield and is never named. Path Maker deals true damage, so the page's armour advice is aimed at the wrong stat. All Out heals him and no anti-heal timing is stated anywhere. Worst of all, mid tells the reader 'never commit your combo into a fresh Defiant Dance' — Defiant Dance is Irelia's own W.
audit.why: A player told to dodge a knockup will position to avoid displacement away from him, when the actual threat drags her back into his range every 3.5 seconds. And the page instructs the player to fear her own ability.
audit.corrected: Q rewritten as the 3.5s slow that shockwave-pulls at two stacks; Path Maker named as the charge-stun and its true damage stated; Footwork named as the shield to force out before committing; All Out's healing given the Grievous Wounds answer; the Defiant Dance mix-up in mid replaced with Path Maker.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with the packet and with this page's own whys: Level 1 read Irelia while whys[0] says you are both soft; Level 3 read K'Sante while whys[2] describes your armour shred melting him; Levels 4-5 read K'Sante while whys[3] literally opens with 'Even window'; First item read K'Sante while whys[5] calls it a coinflip.
audit.why: 49.78% over 918 Emerald+ games is a genuinely even lane that only tips at two items, exactly as the packet chart has it.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3 and 5 flipped in both layers as one atomic group with matching ratings. Level 6 stays Irelia, 2+ items stays K'Sante.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracks All Out on every line without its cooldown, and never gives Ntofo Strikes' cooldown despite it being the ability you eat most often.
audit.why: Ntofo Strikes is 3.5 seconds flat — you cannot wait it out, which is why the correct read is the Path Maker and Footwork cooldowns instead. All Out is 120s at rank 1, a real punish window.
audit.corrected: Q's 3.5s written into spikes[3], Path Maker's charge spend into mid and wants.you[2], Footwork's shield made the thing to force out first.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] and the shred lines treat stacking armour and armour shred as the whole answer to him.
audit.why: Path Maker deals true damage, so resistances do not reduce his single biggest trade-opener, and All Out heals him. Grievous Wounds is the item that actually changes the maths.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal moved into the prose (whys[6]) rather than left as a stray clause in breakdown.late. No claim is made about exact armour values.

edits.before: You're a weak Level 1 with only Bladesurge and no stun, but so is he with just Q — farm with resets off the wave and sidestep his Q knockup.
edits.after: You're weak at Level 1 with only Bladesurge, but so is he with just Ntofo Strikes (Q) — farm resets off the wave and step out of its second-stack pull.

edits.before: His W charge-and-block comes online to eat a trade — don't commit, bait the channel onto the wave first.
edits.after: Path Maker (W) arrives: it charges, cuts the damage he takes, then stuns — bait that channel onto the wave.

edits.before: Even window — he holds W to block your burst and Q-knockups your dash chain, so only trade when his W is down.
edits.after: Even window — he holds Path Maker to eat your burst and Footwork (E) shields the rest, so trade once W is spent.

edits.before: He out-scales hard: a tanked K'Sante ults to isolate you off the wave with no reset target, then out-trades your autos in realm form — close the game before this.
edits.after: He out-scales hard: a tanked K'Sante ults to isolate you off the wave with no reset target, and All Out heals him through your DPS unless you bought Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: His window: a tanked K'Sante ults to isolate you off the wave with no minion or E-mark to reset Bladesurge on, his Q knockup interrupts your dash chain, and the realm-form damage out-trades your ramping autos in a drawn-out 1v1.
edits.after: His window: a tanked K'Sante ults to isolate you off the wave with no minion or E-mark to reset Bladesurge on, Ntofo Strikes drags you back in every 3.5 seconds, and All Out's healing out-lasts your ramping autos in a drawn-out 1v1.

edits.before: Hold Defiant Dance to soak his Q knockup and burst, then E-Q in once his W charge is spent so the damage reduction window isn't up to block you
edits.after: Force Footwork (E) out first — that shield is what eats your burst window — then E-Q in once Path Maker's charge is spent and his damage cut is gone

edits.before: Land his Q knockup to interrupt your Bladesurge dash chain and cut off your reset uptime in extended trades
edits.after: Stack Ntofo Strikes (Q) to shockwave-pull you off the wave and cut your Bladesurge reset uptime in extended trades

edits.before: Level 1 you're both soft, so just farm with Bladesurge off the wave and don't facecheck his Q — its knockup is both a poke and a way to interrupt your dash chain. At Level 2 his W comes online as a charge-and-block channel, so don't throw a raw trade into it; bait it onto minions first. Level 3 is your first real edge: E-stun, Bladesurge in for the reset, stack your passive, and your max-stack armor shred eats a K'Sante who has barely any armor yet — short, sharp trades, then disengage before his W cooldown is back.
edits.after: Level 1 you're both soft, so farm Bladesurge off the wave and stay out of Ntofo Strikes (Q): it slows on a 3.5-second cooldown and its second stack shockwave-pulls you back toward him. At Level 2 Path Maker (W) comes online — he charges, takes reduced damage, then stuns for true damage, so bait that channel onto minions before you trade. Level 3 is your first real edge: E-stun, Bladesurge in for the reset, stack your passive, and shred a K'Sante with barely any armour yet — short trades, out before W is back.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay even — he can hold W to block your burst and Q-knockup your dash, so look for trades when his W is on cooldown rather than forcing every wave. Level 6 is your window: Vanguard's Edge drops a wall behind him so he can't W-dash out of your reset chain, and a full max-stack all-in beats a K'Sante who hasn't bought tank items yet. Bait the W charge, E in once it's spent, and never commit your combo into a fresh Defiant Dance.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay even — he holds Path Maker to eat your burst and Footwork shields whatever gets through, so trade when both are down rather than every wave. Level 6 is your window: Vanguard's Edge drops a wall behind him so he can't dash out of your reset chain, and a full max-stack all-in beats a K'Sante who hasn't bought tank items yet. Bait the Path Maker charge, E in once it's spent, and never dump your combo into a fresh Footwork shield.

notes: Biggest correction: seven strings called Ntofo Strikes a knockup. Riot's text has it slowing and, at two stacks, PULLING enemies in — the reader was being taught to fear displacement in the wrong direction. The knockback/stun is Path Maker. mid also told the player not to commit into a fresh 'Defiant Dance', which is Irelia's own W, not K'Sante's. Path Maker's true damage means armour is not the answer to his opener, and All Out's healing means Grievous Wounds is; both are now on the page. Four chart rows flipped as a matched group to agree with the packet and the page's own whys.
